from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Pulse of Time", [
            "Time flows in a constant steady pulse.",
            "We call each unit a beat.",
            "Imagine these as equally spaced dots."
        ])
        
        # Animations
        time_line = Line(start=self.grid['D1'], end=self.grid['D6'], color="#00FF00")
        beats = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#FFFFFF") for _ in range(6)])
        for i, beat in enumerate(beats):
            beat.move_to(self.grid[f'D{i+1}'])
            
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(time_line), FadeIn(beats))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(beats.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        for beat in beats:
            beat.set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Concept of Measures (Bars)", ["Measures group beats into containers.", "Bar lines divide the rhythm.", "Each box holds steady beats."])
        
        # --- Elements ---
        measure_box = Rectangle(width=4.0, height=1.5, color=WHITE)
        bar_lines = VGroup(
            Line(UP * 0.75, DOWN * 0.75, color="#00FFFF"),
            Line(UP * 0.75, DOWN * 0.75, color="#00FFFF"),
            Line(UP * 0.75, DOWN * 0.75, color="#00FFFF")
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.0)
        
        beats = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color="#FF8000", fill_opacity=1) for _ in range(4)])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.place_in_area(measure_box, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.0)))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Position bar lines inside the box
        center_area = self.grid['C3']
        bar_lines.move_to(center_area)
        self.play(Create(bar_lines))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        beats.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5).move_to(center_area)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(b) for b in beats], lag_ratio=0.2))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF8000")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Decoding the Time Signature", [
            "Time signatures act as maps.", 
            "The top number counts beats.", 
            "The bottom shows note values.", 
            "Whole notes split into parts.", 
            "Four beats fill one measure."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        fraction = MathTex(r"{4 \over 4}", font_size=96)
        top_num = fraction[0][0]
        bottom_num = fraction[0][2]
        
        self.place_at_grid(fraction, 'C3', scale_factor=1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(fraction))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(top_num.animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(bottom_num.animate.set_color("#0000FF"))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#0000FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Sector uses 'radius' instead of 'outer_radius' in basic instantiation
        pie = VGroup(
            Sector(radius=1.0, angle=PI/2, start_angle=0, color=RED),
            Sector(radius=1.0, angle=PI/2, start_angle=PI/2, color=GREEN),
            Sector(radius=1.0, angle=PI/2, start_angle=PI, color=BLUE),
            Sector(radius=1.0, angle=PI/2, start_angle=3*PI/2, color=YELLOW)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(pie, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(pie))
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(fraction.animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Measures create rhythmic hierarchy.",
            "Beat one is the downbeat.",
            "It acts as the accent.",
            "Higher bounces signify the downbeat.",
            "Marching keeps the squad synchronized."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Dynamic Application: The Accent Pattern", lecture_lines)
        
        # Bouncing balls to represent beats
        balls = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.6) for _ in range(4)])
        self.place_at_grid(balls[0], 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(balls[1], 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(balls[2], 'C4')
        self.place_at_grid(balls[3], 'C5')
        
        self.add(balls)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(balls[0].animate.set_color(ORANGE).scale(1.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(RED))
        # Animate "bounce" for the accent
        self.play(Indicate(balls[0], scale_factor=1.5, color=ORANGE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(TEAL))
        # Final rhythm animation
        for ball in balls:
            self.play(ball.animate.shift(UP*0.5).shift(DOWN*0.5), run_time=0.3)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", [
            "Beats create the pulse.",
            "Measures build the structure.",
            "Signatures act as blueprints.",
            "Geometric shapes show rhythmic variety.",
            "Rhythm follows clear mathematical rules."
        ])

        # Assets
        pulse = Dot(color=BLUE).scale(2)
        measure = Rectangle(height=1.5, width=2.5, color=GREEN)
        blueprint = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT, RIGHT), Line(UP, DOWN)
        ).set_color(YELLOW)

        # Position assets
        self.place_at_grid(pulse, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(measure, "C4")
        self.place_at_grid(blueprint, "E3")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Indicate(pulse))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(Indicate(measure))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Indicate(blueprint))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        # Add visual shapes
        tri = Triangle(color=ORANGE).scale(0.5)
        sq = Square(color=RED).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(tri, "A5")
        self.place_at_grid(sq, "B5")
        self.play(FadeIn(tri), FadeIn(sq))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(FadeOut(pulse), FadeOut(measure), FadeOut(blueprint), FadeOut(tri), FadeOut(sq))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Architecture of Rhythm: Music and Measure Theory

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Pulse of Time
sections.content: Establish the concept of 'Beat' as a constant, periodic unit of time. Introduce the visual representation of beats as equidistant dots on a timeline.
sections.example: A metronome ticking steadily or a robotic drum-bot tapping its foot at a constant speed.

sections.title: The Concept of Measures (Bars)
sections.content: Introduce 'Measures' as containers that group beats. Explain the 'Bar Line' as a vertical wall that divides the infinite timeline into manageable chunks.
sections.example: Think of a conveyor belt carrying boxes. Each box (measure) contains exactly 4 rhythmic items (beats) before the next box begins.

sections.title: Decoding the Time Signature
sections.content: Explain the fraction-like notation (e.g., 4/4). Top number = beats per measure; Bottom number = note value of the beat. Use a pie-chart animation to show how a whole note splits into parts.
sections.example: In 4/4 time, imagine a hungry caterpillar that must eat exactly 4 'leaf-beats' before moving to the next segment of the branch.

sections.title: Dynamic Application: The Accent Pattern
sections.content: Explain how measure theory creates hierarchy. Beat 1 is always the 'strong' beat (the downbeat). Visualize this with a bouncing ball—the first bounce is highest.
sections.example: A marching band: The 'LEFT-right-left-right' pattern is dictated by the measure, where the first step is emphasized to keep the squad synchronized.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Recap: Beats provide the pulse, measures provide the structure, and time signatures act as the mathematical blueprint. Challenge students to identify the time signature of a short auditory clip.
sections.example: A snippet of a waltz (3/4) vs. a rock beat (4/4) visualized as repeating geometric shapes: triangles (3 beats) vs. squares (4 beats).
